subject: Learning Methods
title: When External Rewards Work
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on When External Rewards Work.

hook.text: A hospital paid staff for hand washing compliance. Rates jumped from 10 % to 90 %. Some tasks need external push.

buildup.text: External rewards work best for tasks that are boring, unpleasant, or require initial effort before becoming rewarding.

discovery.text: The key is using rewards as a bridge. Start with external incentives, then gradually shift motivation to internal.

twist.text: Tangible rewards (money, prizes) are risky. Informational rewards (feedback, progress markers) tend to enhance.

climax.text: Use small rewards to start difficult habits. Track your streaks. Then let the growing competence become its own reward.

punchline.text: Rewards bridge the gap. Competence takes over after.

quiz.question: When are external rewards most effective for learning?
options: When the learner is already highly motivated
For initially boring or unpleasant tasks that need a motivational bridge
When the reward is as large as possible
